perspective:
Ethan’s available information:

- He knows Gary Guo is his long-time friend from middle school; Gary is a doctor, and they have a close, supportive friendship.
- He noticed Gary working excessively long hours at the hospital, often skipping meals and sacrificing sleep. This concerned him.
- He invited Gary to a weekend retreat for relaxation/rejuvenation, saying Gary’s health mattered, he hated seeing Gary like this, and two days might give him a new perspective.
- He heard Gary initially decline, saying he appreciated the concern but couldn’t because there was too much to do at the hospital.
- At the retreat, he observed Gary being restless and avoiding discussions about work. Ethan suspected there was more to Gary’s overworking than just professional obligations.
- He confronted Gary, saying they had been friends since middle school, Gary could tell him anything, and he was there to help, not judge.
- He heard Gary say it was complicated and that he didn’t want to burden Ethan.
- After the confrontation, Gary opened up to Ethan about pressures managing a new department and personal challenges. Ethan felt relief and empathy.
- Ethan suggested prioritizing tasks and delegating responsibilities. He heard Gary agree and say he could use help organizing his schedule to make time for himself.
- Over the following months, Ethan regularly checked in with Gary, discussed his progress and challenges, saw Gary making efforts to change, and felt hopeful and proud.
- Ethan told Gary he was proud of his progress and available whenever Gary needed to talk. He heard Gary say things were better, that Ethan’s help meant he was less overwhelmed, and that he had time for a movie last weekend.
- After a year, Ethan saw Gary managing on his own and felt satisfied and happy for him. He decided to step back, telling Gary he was always a call away but knew Gary had this.
- He heard Gary thank him, say he couldn’t have done it without Ethan’s support, and that he felt more in control now.
